#1694. Lorient vs Rennes - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 20 Nov 2026 18:32, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 18:38

Lorient will aim to extend a superb run against their Breton neighbours Rennes, who make the short trip to the Stade du Moustoir on Sunday afternoon.

Sitting 10th in the Ligue 1 table on 15 points from 10 outings (W4, D3, L3), the hosts trail the eighth-placed visitors by a single point, with the Red and Blacks themselves just one adrift of sixth-placed Nice.

Lorient go into the derby in good heart, having taken three wins, a draw and a loss from their last five league fixtures while keeping four shutouts, which lifts their tally to a division-high six this season.

Alexandre Dujeux’s team bounced back from a disappointing loss against Brest on home soil by securing 2-0 victory away at Le Havre before the international break, thanks to strikes from Isaak Toure and Jean-Victor Makengo.

That success was only the second time all season that the Morbihan side have netted more than once in a match, in a campaign shaped by a cautious approach that has produced a league-low 17 goals across their fixtures.

Lorient’s tally of nine strikes in Ligue 1 this term is the joint-poorest in the top flight, alongside two of the bottom three sides in Angers and Le Havre, though only Lille (seven) have shipped fewer than the Merlus’ eight.

Interestingly, three-quarters of those eight concessions have come at Stade du Moustoir, where both of their wins from five games (D1. L2) season have arrived with a clean sheet, so another watertight showing would be crucial on Sunday.

Even so, Lorient can approach the contest with belief, having beaten Rennes in each of the past six meetings, including a 6-0 aggregate triumph across both league encounters in 2025-26, four of those goals arriving at home.

That makes this a daunting assignment for the visitors, who have lost three of their last five in the French top flight (W2), and went down 2-1 at home to Les Dogues in their most recent outing.

Franck Haise’s team briefly led Ligue 1 after a 3-0 win over Strasbourg in October, but subsequent defeats by Nice and Lille mean they have collected only one victory from six games in all competitions.

In Europe, however, Rennes are unbeaten through four fixtures this term, having drawn the last two, and sit 17th in the Europa League standings ahead of a Matchday 5 trip to NEC next Thursday, once this Brittany derby is done.

There is little doubt that Haise’s charges boast a greater attacking threat than this weekend’s hosts, having scored 21 times in the league, but their defensive record has been a major worry, with the same number shipped, which is more than any side in the top half.

The Red and Blacks have also struggled on their travels, losing each of their last three away games in Ligue 1 and conceding at least four times in every one, a run that is worth bearing in mind when comparing goals markets at the best new betting sites UK.

Lorient are expected to be without Isaak Toure, who picked up an adductor knock during the win at Le Havre and reportedly faces a spell on the sidelines.

Right wing-back Panos Katseris also remains unavailable because of a muscle complaint that has kept him out since September, while midfielder Bandiougou Fadiga is back in training after a hamstring problem and could be in contention.

Ibrahima Balde is fit again after recovering from an Achilles injury, although Souleymane Mame Faye could still be deployed in a two-man support act alongside Makengo behind striker Mamadou Kone.

For the visitors, right-back Przemyslaw Frankowski is doubtful after leaving the Poland camp over the international break with a muscular strain.

Rennes are, however, boosted  by the return of leading marksman Esteban Lepaul, who has netted seven times in the league and could spearhead the attack beside Boulaye Dia after shaking off an ankle issue.

Mvogo; Talbi, Adjei, Obaretin; Sylla, Avom, Cadiou, Kouassi; Faye, Makengo; Kone

Samba; Cresswell, Ait Boudlal, Oliveira; Reynolds, Rongier, Thomasson, Szymanski, Nagida; Dia, Lepaul

A watertight rearguard and a fine record in this derby should leave Dujeux’s men brimming with confidence, particularly after that encouraging success on the road at Le Havre.

However, Rennes carry far greater attacking quality, and Lepaul’s return could help them end a losing streak away from home, even if a share of the spoils looks likelier than a full haul.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Then, Koni De Winter repeated similar sentiments today, saying that he may be a little crazy, but he was a good character to be around and a great footballer and Milan fans can see this, too. “Working with Allegri was beneficial for me. It’s under his guidance that I’ve made the most progress since arriving in Italy. As a central defender, I possess good speed, strength, and skill with the ball.

“I can pass the ball forward and score goals, but tactical skills have always been a weakness of mine. I only learned the basics when I joined the first team at Partizan. The bond that unites Moreira and Pavlovic…

“I didn’t even know he was Almami’s son [a former Partizan player]. He’s a fantastic guy, really smart. He knows a few bits of Serbian. I met his father during a training session. We talked about Partizan, of course. It was really nice to see him; I remember him from his time at Partizan.”

The possibility of joining Partizan at the end of his career…

“I often joke with Moreira, telling him that, at the end of our careers, we should play at least one season at Partizan. I point out that I’m three years older than him, so he’ll have to make a small sacrifice so we can get back together. He’s a truly great guy.

A deal has already been agreed for an African sensation who people should not forget about.

Football comes in waves. It ebbs and flows. From one generation to another. Giants are born and giants are toppled. A club like Liverpool has ebbed and flowed a lot more than others over the years.

There was a golden era in the 1970s and 1980s, followed by bleak and dark times, succeeded by even darker times on the pitch barring one miracle night in Istanbul.

Then along game the beacon of hope. Jurgen Klopp restored the faith at the club and took Liverpool back to the apex of the footballing world.

Now it's Andoni Iraola's job to sort out the mess he inherited from Arne Slot and follow in the footsteps of Klopp.

What Julian Ward is planning to make Liverpool the best team in the worldOf course, it's never just the head-coach who is responsible, especially these days in modern football. But most notably, Liverpool have ventured to different continents in order to complete signings. Samuel Martinez was recruited from Colombia. Meanwhile, Mor Talla Ndiaye has been signed from Senegal. #1691. Augsburg vs Mainz 05 - prediction, team news, lineups

By Lewis Nolan | 20 Nov 2026 18:34, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 19:54

Augsburg's WWK Arena will be the backdrop for their clash with Mainz 05 on Sunday in a potentially pivotal clash in the battle against relegation.

The home side are 14th in the Bundesliga table with nine points, whereas their opponents are 12th with 10, and a loss for either could leave them in the bottom three.

Augsburg are only two points above 16th-placed Union Berlin, who occupy the relegation playoff spot, while they are just three points ahead of 17th-placed Schalke 04.

The hosts are winless in their past seven league matches, a period in which they claimed just three points and suffered four defeats.

Head coach Manuel Baum will not be pleased that his team conceded at least two goals in six of those fixtures, though he will highlight that the club netted 13 times in that stretch.

Fuggerstadter have played five contests at WWK Arena in 2026-27, and they have triumphed once, drawn three times and won once at the stadium.

Two of those stalemates came against Bayern Munich and Bayer Leverkusen, while their only defeat at home came against third-placed Freiburg at the end of October.

The visitors come into the clash looking to avoid a fifth consecutive loss in all competitions, and avoid losing a fourth straight Bundesliga game.

Perhaps the saving grace for Mainz is that the rest of the bottom seven play teams currently in the top eight, meaning it is unlikely that they will end the weekend in the relegation zone.

Urs Fischer's side did score four goals in their four losses, but they conceded on 11 occasions, and their latest defeat saw them ship twice when they lost 2-1 against Bayern Munich on November 7.

Mainz's record on the road has been largely positive this term, as while they were beaten 4-1 by Elversberg on October 30, they did emerge as winners in their first three away Bundesliga outings of the campaign.

The club are also unbeaten in their five most recent meetings with Augsburg, claiming victory four times, including when they won 2-0 in February.

Augsburg only have two confirmed absentees, with Han-Noah Massengo and defender Chrislain Matsima ruled out.

Juma Bah, Jeffrey Gouweleeuw and Yannik Keitel could be trusted together in defence, while Robin Fellhauer and Fabian Rieder may start in a double pivot.

Striker Michael Gregoritsch has scored five times in the league this season, and he is certain to lead the line, supported by Anton Kade and Alexis Claude-Maurice.

Though Mainz only have to contend with the absence of centre-back Dominik Kohr, he is not scheduled to return until January because of an ankle injury.

Stefan Posch, Fabio Gruber and Kacper Potulski are likely candidates to start in the team's back three, and the trio may be protected by Paul Nebel and Kaishu Sano from midfield.

Dahmen; Bah, Gouweleeuw, Keitel; Wolf, Fellhauer, Rieder, Behrens; Kade, Claude-Maurice; Gregoritsch

Zentner; Posch, Gruber, Potulski; Caci, Nebel, Sano, Amiri, Mwene; Tietz, Becker

Neither Augsburg nor Mainz have been particularly strong defensively, so it would be surprising if either kept a clean sheet.

The hosts boast the advantage of playing at WWK Arena, but the visitors have often travelled well, and the two may ultimately have to settle for a point on Sunday.

#1690. Sonia Bompastor's side show their teeth as Chelsea sink the reigning champions to reclaim top spot in WSL title race: Chelsea 1-0 Man City

By SAMARA WATTS and TARA ANSON-WALSH, FOOTBALL REPORTER

Published: 10:42 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 11:33 EST, 15 November 2026

Chelsea secured a deserved 1-0 victory over Manchester City at Stamford Bridge to leapfrog their rivals and reclaim top spot in the WSL table.

Sandy Baltimore's first-half goal was enough to ensure Chelsea inflicted City's first defeat of the season and blow the title race wide open.

After keeping the reigning WSL champions at bay following an early barrage, Chelsea grew in confidence but still lacked the cutting edge that had seen them held to back-to-back draws in the past week.

A moment of magic from Baltimore in the fourth minute of stoppage time ensured history would not repeat itself.

City goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita was sent off in the 75th minute for a rash challenge on Alyssa Thompson, a move which appeared to invigorate the visitors, but Chelsea held firm to pick up all three points.

Daily Mail Sport's Tara Anson-Walsh and Samara Watts were at Stamford Bridge to bring you the things we learned...

Chelsea inflicted City's first defeat of the season and blew the title race wide open

City goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita was sent off in the 75th minute for a rash challenge on Alyssa Thompson

Devastation for Kadeisha Buchanan, who was hooked after 11 minutes by Bompastor. The centre back has been one of Chelsea’s standout performers this season but had an unusually shaky start to this match as she looked out of her depth against Bunny Shaw, ever a precarious place to be against the league’s top striker.

Buchanan gave an early ball away to allow Shaw to race through towards the Chelsea goal, and a few minutes later was again outmuscled and outpaced by the Jamaican striker, although City failed to capitalise on both occasions.

The 31-year-old Canada international looked devastated when her number flashed up on the board after just 12 minutes and reluctantly welcomed a hug from her manager as she headed straight for the tunnel.

Her replacement, the 20-year-old Veerle Buurman, who was outstanding against Shaw in the two sides’ last meeting in the FA Cup last season, changed the game, giving Chelsea a more solid platform to build upon as they grew in confidence.

Bompastor shut down suggestions that the move had been ruthlessly tactical at full time, saying that Buchanan had picked up a head injury during training on Friday.

'She was fine after the training session, she was fine in the evening and we assessed her again this morning and everything was fine,' Bompastor said.

'I had this information on what happened yesterday and I just felt, watching her from the beginning of the game, she was not herself. I took the responsibility to make this substitution. I was almost forced to do that because, I know my player, and I know she was not right in the game.'

For those sceptical, it certainly improved things.

The centre back has been one of Chelsea’s standout performers this season but had an unusually shaky start to this match and was hooked after just 11 minutes

Women’s football royalty Sarina Wiegman and Emma Hayes braved the chilly climes of Stamford Bridge to witness the showdown between the WSL heavyweights on Saturday afternoon.

The freshly anointed honorary Dame Wiegman sat next to Hayes and the pair chatted warmly, with Wiegman laughing as Hayes attempted to encourage her to celebrate Chelsea's victory at full time. This is a relationship that will no doubt drop in cordiality as the sand in the hourglass ahead of next summer’s World Cup continues to run down.

Wiegman had several England players on her watching brief, not least young Lexi Potter, whose stock has risen dramatically this season. The 20-year-old put in another assured performance against the reigning champions, continuing to demonstrate her maturity in the highest stakes, which will no doubt put her in a good position ahead of Tuesday’s squad announcement.

Elsewhere, the Dutch coach will have been alarmed by the number of crunching tackles put in against her right back, Lucy Bronze, in this match. If there is one player that she will want to wrap up in cotton wool ahead of Brazil, it is the recently turned 35-year-old Bronze for her steadfast leadership and relentless athleticism.

One player looking to make an impact ahead of Tuesday’s squad announcement was Aggie Beever-Jones, who has struggled this season and was left out of Sonia Bompastor’s starting line-up. An injury to Melvine Malard saw Beever-Jones gain more minutes than she would have expected, but it felt like another afternoon of deja vu for the 23-year-old forward as she failed to convert a number of chances despite finding herself in good positions.

Meanwhile, in Manchester, Ella Toone's hopes of forcing her way back into Sarina Wiegman's plans suffered another blow as the 27-year-old was once again left out of Eva Olid's starting line-up for United's 2-0 win over Crystal Palace. Toone watched on as fellow Lioness Maya Le Tissier opened the scoring with a superb long-range strike, and the two-time European champion will no doubt be growing increasingly concerned as Brazil draws closer.

The freshly anointed honorary dame Wiegman sat next to Hayes at the WSL showpiece at Stamford Bridge and the pair chatted warmly

Melvine Malard’s absence raises questions about who Chelsea’s main goalscorer will be this season. The squad has lacked a clinical edge without England striker Lauren James, who is out with a hamstring injury until the international break.

The French forward went off injured after 35 minutes with a suspected hamstring injury. Although she missed Chelsea’s opening games after picking up a knock in pre-season, she has been the Blues’ top scorer in the absence of Lauren James with six league goals so far.

Chelsea are averaging 24 shots per game, an unprecedented rate across a WSL campaign, but have recently struggled to convert their chances. They were held to a 0-0 draw against BK Hacken midweek in the UWCL and a 1-1 draw against Everton last weekend.

Malard leaving the pitch meant Chelsea struggled to find a creative spark up front. Her replacement Aggie Beever-Jones has been dealing with an ankle injury, and is still trying to find her feet with only one goal in the WSL.

Head coach Bompastor said: ‘The frustration sometimes comes from us not being ruthless and clinical.’

A moment of magic from Malard’s French international teammate Sandy Baltimore was enough to make it 1-0 just before half time with the team’s first shot on target. However, Baltimore was substituted at half time to manage her minutes, and Chelsea were unable to capitalize on any of their chances in the second half.

Bompastor said: ‘From the outside it seems like we have had a lot of injuries, but we have been playing every three days.’

‘I knew coming into the game we were not as fresh as we would like to be, but that’s our environment.

‘We want to play in every competition but the players are not robots,’

Melvine Malard’s injury could cause more problems for the Blues’ attack, as they registered just two shots on target today and scraped the three points.

Malard limped off in the first half and meant Chelsea struggled for a creative spark up front

Stamford Bridge was in uproar as City goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita rushed out of her box and took down Alyssa Thompson, who had a clear chance on goal in the 75th minute.

The Blues were mounting a rapid attack down the left hand side, with Thompson just outside the box when Yamashita missed the ball and brought her to the ground.

The Japanese goalkeeper was shown a straight red card and was sent off the pitch. This was City’s first red card in the WSL since November 2023, and a rare moment of madness from the usually-composed 31-year-old.

The referee allowed City three minutes to replace the Japanese goalkeeper, with Scotland’s number one Eartha Cumings coming on to replace forward Aoba Fujino.

Her first test arrived only a minute later, as Aggie Beever-Jones' right-footed shot from the resulting indirect free kick dropped dangerously, but she was saved by the crossbar.

The bigger question now is whether Yamashita's absence - which could amass to three games - will have a lasting impact on their title race.

In the short-term against Chelsea, City reacted well. Andree Jeglertz said at full time: ‘The players dealt with it in a good way, so even though we were one player down we had a couple of great opportunities to score a goal. Of course it affected the game but that is not why we lost.’

Stamford Bridge was in uproar as Manchester City goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita rushed out of her box to take down Alyssa Thompson, who had a clear chance on goal

Chelsea’s win at the Bridge blows the title race wide open, as they are now just one point ahead of City at the top of the WSL table.

Bompastor’s side ended City’s unbeaten streak, and they now have 24 league goals compared to City’s 16 after 10 games.

However, with seven shots and just one on target this game, Chelsea will need to look at their attacking options as they take on Liverpool and London City Lionesses before the international break.

Bompastor said: ‘It’s a nice feeling to be top of the table right now and to win against these top sides, but I know we still have a lot of work to be done and it’s early on in the season so many things can happen.’

City were unable to create opportunities in front of goal, with the WSL’s all-time leading goalscorer Vivianne Miedema’s return overshadowed by Ayaka Yamashita’s nightmare in goal.

City head coach Andree Jeglertz said: ‘They managed to score on their big chance and (it was a) great finish.

'We also had some great opportunities where we didn’t manage to score, but I think we deserve more than going away from here with no points.’

London City Lionesses face Arsenal tomorrow at the Emirates, and a win in north London could bring them four points behind the new WSL leaders, and really start to make things interesting.

#1689. Opinion: Real Madrid announce deal and now the door is open for incredible Liverpool move

The door is undoubtedly open for Liverpool to strike an incredible move. Real Madrid opened that door with a deal announcement.

Liverpool need to boost their midfield. That's apparent to all, even after striking two big-money contract deals with Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai this year.

But do either actually get into Liverpool's first-XI right now? Virtually everyone would pick Trey Nyoni and Alexis Mac Allister at the pairing and that absolutely was not the plan for the campaign.

Nyoni is an interesting one, though. He's proven that Liverpool look better with a proper defensive, controlling midfielder in there - something most people figured would be the case before the summer.

Liverpool, however, did not believe that. They didn't sign any midfielders and instead sold Curtis Jones without replacing him, leaving the squad short and over-reliant on attack-first options in the middle.

Nyoni has shown that Liverpool were wrong. Of course, it looks like they'd already figured that out by the end of August, with moves for midfielders quickly heading to the top of their agenda for 2027 after just a few games this season.

And we don't expect Liverpool to rely so heavily on Nyoni for the entirety of the campaign. He does need some degree of help and the midfield could use a reshuffle.

Eduardo Camavinga looks possiblePut it all together and a move for Eduardo Camavinga looks like it should be high-priority for Liverpool. The Frenchman is one of the best defensive midfielders on the planet, even if Real Madrid don't quite rely on him all that much. Our Value Adder model suggests Camavinga is very, very underrated and the reason for that is largely Aurelien Tchouameni. Tchouameni might be the world's best defensive midfielder, honestly, and casts an enormous shadow over his compatriot.

Put it all together and a move for Eduardo Camavinga looks like it should be high-priority for Liverpool. The Frenchman is one of the best defensive midfielders on the planet, even if Real Madrid don't quite rely on him all that much.

Our Value Adder model suggests Camavinga is very, very underrated and the reason for that is largely Aurelien Tchouameni. Tchouameni might be the world's best defensive midfielder, honestly, and casts an enormous shadow over his compatriot.

That's why Camavinga hasn't entirely established himself at Real Madrid and why certain clubs were pushing to sign him in the summer. He decided to stay put, however, and we imagine that was to try and force his way in under Jose Mourinho.

That hasn't happened. Camavinga has only started two La Liga fixtures and reports suggest they hold interest in signing Martin Zubimendi. That's a signing that would usurp Camavinga.

More than that, Real Madrid have doubled-down on Tchouameni, committing to a big new contract this week. There's essentially no way for Camavinga to get into that starting XI regularly - and the new contract confirms that.

Which is why we feel the door is now open pretty wide for Liverpool. Camavinga is a fantastic, high-energy player who could be exactly what the Reds need to improve their midfield. The opportunity looks to be there and they should try to take it.

According to Fabrizio Romano, AC Milan could be involved in the market for Alejandro Balde once again this winter.

A central defender would be the main target for most Milan fans ahead of the winter mercato, but the possibility of signing another wing-back wouldn’t be turned down. In fact, with the left-side still proving to be a puzzling area, someone may need to be recruited.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In the past, Balde has been linked and there have been several other suggestions. However, the Spaniard may be the most accessible mid-way through the season and it would seem that the Rossoneri are considering him again.

Speaking on his YouTube channel, Romano looked at the left-back’s future and didn’t deny that the Diavolo could be involved for another mercato, as MilanNews relayed.

“In the last few hours, Barcelona’s sporting director Deco spoke about Alejandro Balde and said that they are not planning on Balde’s exit because we are only in mid-November; there is a month and a half to go until January.

#1687. Inside Sir Alex Ferguson's inner circle of Man United legends: The player threatened 'he will end up in a ditch' by football chief, the cult-hero striker still playing at 38 and sorry Michael Carrick after his Old Trafford sacking

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 02:01 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 11:52 EST, 15 November 2026

It's safe to say Manchester United are going through a rough patch - and then some - at the moment, but many of their supporters would have raised a smile at one photo that surfaced earlier this month.

A few of the club's legends reunited to raise a glass to Sir Alex Ferguson on his 40th anniversary of being named Red Devils manager.

Ferguson, who retired in 2013, won 38 major honours during a trophy-laden 26 years at Old Trafford.

And as the 84-year-old received plaudits across the footballing world, he enjoyed a celebratory intimate setting with some of his former players and actor James Nesbitt in Manchester.

Diehard United fan Nesbitt shared a group photo on Instagram, featuring Ferguson alongside Michael Carrick, Edwin van der Sar, Nemanja Vidic, Robin van Persie, Darren Fletcher, Jonny Evans, Javier Hernandez and John O'Shea.

But what are those former United players up to now? Daily Mail Sport takes a look...

Actor and Man United fan James Nesbitt (centre right) posted this picture with club royalty - clockwise from front left: Jonny Evans, Darren Fletcher, Robin van Persie, Nemanja Vidic, Michael Carrick, John O'Shea, Sir Alex Ferguson, Edwin van der Sar and Javier Hernandez

Unless you've been on another planet, then you would know everything about Carrick this past week.

The 45-year-old was sacked as United head coach on Thursday morning after a disastrous start to the season.

Carrick, who has been replaced by Mauricio Pochettino, oversaw United's worst top-flight start since Ferguson replaced Ron Atkinson 40 years ago - with one victory in 10 Premier League matches as they sit 18th.

Furthermore this season, he only won three of 15 games in all competitions.

The downturn in the Red Devils' form is bewildering considering their upturn when Carrick replaced Ruben Amorim in mid-January last season. He was handed a two-year contract in May after guiding United to a third-place finish and qualification for the Champions League, losing just two of his 17 games as head coach.

Carrick was sacked as Manchester United head coach on Thursday morning by club chiefs

He oversaw United's worst top-flight start in Premier League history with one win in 10 games

Like Carrick, Evans is also out of a job having been part of his backroom staff at United as first-team coach.

After retiring as a player at the end of the 2024-25 season, Evans took up the position of head of loans and pathways at Carrington but left that role last December.

Following Amorim's sacking he returned to the club to help Fletcher during his caretaker manager stint before being kept on by Carrick.

Like Carrick, Evans was relieved of his United duties having been part of his backroom team

The sole former player still connected directly with the club, Fletcher is their Under 18s head coach. The Scot had to pause his role last season when becoming the club's first-team interim head coach following Amorim's sacking in January - drawing 2-2 with Burnley in the Premier League before overseeing their FA Cup third-round home defeat by Brighton a few days later.

Having come through the club's academy, Fletcher knows what it takes to make the grade at the club and has the likes of Kai Rooney, son of Wayne, and Jacey Carrick, son of Michael, among his squad.

And Fletcher's young charges are enjoying a strong start to the season which has included six goals in wins over Liverpool (6-3) and Burnley (6-0) at the end of last month.

Fletcher is the Red Devils' U18s head coach - nurturing the club's latest crop of rising stars

The former Red Devils captain had ambitions to go into coaching, having done his badges, but has turned his focus on building up a real estate portfolio - telling Gary Neville on The Overlap last July that he had put £4.5million into building 76 one or two-bedroom apartments in Belgrade, Serbia.

However, this summer it was reported that Vidic had been a previous target of intimidation by a former football chief.

According to Serbian media, encrypted messages show then-Serbia's football president Slavisa Kokeza wanted people to threaten Vidic after he had publicly criticised the Serbian Football Association (FSS) over the national side's failure to qualify for the Euro 2020 tournament.

In the reported devised plot in 2020, Kokeza reportedly told one contact to make it clear to Vidic that he should 'stay away from the association or he will end up in a ditch'.

As well as that, criminals were hired to monitor the former centre-back's movements in Milan, where he lived, and fit his car with a tracking device.

Following the revelations, Vidic and his legal team filed a criminal complaint and sought an investigation into the claimed plot.

'In mid-May, OCCRP and KRIK visited my home and told me they had obtained encrypted messages from Sky ECC (a now-defunct communication encryption service which EUROPOL said was widely used by criminals and was broken into by European police in 2021) and analysed them,' Vidic told The Athletic in July.

'The messages were said to have come from the then-president of the SFF in 2020. They were about me and how to stop me from talking to the media. At the time, I was commentating on the situation in Serbian football. I was living in Milan, Italy, where I stayed after finishing my career with Inter. I hadn't yet moved back to Serbia, where I am from and where I live.'

Vidic, who has turned his focus on building up a real estate portfolio, was reportedly a previous target of intimidation by a former football chief

Van der Sar's calm persona on the football pitch translated well into the boardroom during his near-seven-year stint at Ajax as their chief executive officer.

The former Manchester United goalkeeper joined the Dutch giants' board in 2012, becoming CEO in 2016. During his spell Ajax reached the 2017 Europa League final and 2019 Champions League semi-finals with a young exciting core of players including the likes of Frenkie de Jong and Matthijs de Ligt.

The year Van der Sar left though Ajax finished third that season to qualify for the Europa League play-offs, missing out on the Champions League for the first time since 2009.

A few weeks later in July 2023, Van der Sar was put in intensive care after suffering a brain haemorrhage while on holiday in Croatia.

Three years on since recovering, Van der Sar is enjoying being away from football for the time being telling The Overlap in February: 'Now it's almost three years ago, so I've had time to recover with no stress, no phone in my hand - just doing the stuff that I've wanted to do.

'Wake up when you want, walk the dog, go swim in the sea, go on holiday. I went to New Zealand for two months with [wife] Annemarie - nice things that I never had the chance to do before.

'I started playing at 18 or 19, finished at 40, and at 41 I became one of the directors at Ajax until 53, so I thought it was the right time to take a step back. That's taken a little bit longer than I originally thought, to be fair, but we are enjoying ourselves very much.'

Van der Sar was Ajax CEO for seven years before stepping down from the role in 2023

The ex-goalkeeper is now enjoying life with wife Annemarie after a brain haemorrhage in 2023

Like Carrick, Van Persie has turned his hand to first-team management since retiring.

His first role was with Dutch outfit Heerenveen - signing a two-year contract with the club ahead of the 2024-25 season. However, his time there lasted just nine months as he took over the reins at Dutch giants Feyenoord.

However, his time in Rotterdam lasted just 16 months there when he was sacked in June. He had guided them to second in the Eredivisie but they finished 19 points behind champions PSV Eindhoven.

In explaining his sacking, newly-appointed technical director Devy Rigaux cited the style of play as a factor.

'We conducted a thorough internal analysis,' he said. 'In this, we took into account, among other things, the development of the style of play and the declining trend in terms of points total, both in Europe and in the Eredivisie.

'The conclusion was that it is better to start the next season with a new head coach.'

The 43-year-old is awaiting a new job, like Carrick.

Van Persie is currently without a managerial job after being sacked by Feyenoord in June

The sole player from this list to still be playing, Hernandez made history by becoming the first-ever player signed to USL Championship outfit Atletico Dallas.

In July, the 38-year-old penned a two-year deal with an option for a third year at the expansion club which will play in the second-tier of US football, below Major League Soccer.

The Mexican striker still has a few months to wait for his debut though, with the season not beginning until March 2027.

In the meantime, he was part of the FOX broadcast team for the recent World Cup in the United States, Mexico and Canada, serving as an analyst.

Last year, Hernandez was caught up in a sexism storm, which he later apologised for, after he made a series of statements on TikTok 'promoting sexist stereotypes that are considered media violence and go against gender equality in sport'.

Hernandez said women are 'failing' and 'eradicating masculinity'.

'Don't be afraid to be women, to allow yourselves to be led by a man,' said the former Mexico captain on social media.

His remarks sparked a backlash, which led to his apology which included him saying: 'I deeply regret any confusion or discomfort that my recent words have caused.'

Hernandez was fined and warned about his future conduct.

Hernandez, who attended United's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on November 8, is the only player still playing and has signed for USL Championship outfit Atletico Dallas ahead of their new term

Like the majority of the names here, O'Shea's post-playing career has seen him turn to coaching with his current role being the Republic of Ireland assistant head coach.

The 45-year-old has been in this position since August 2024, staying on with his homeland's setup following the appointment of Heimir Hallgrimsson as manager.

O'Shea took charge of the team for four friendly fixtures that year following Stephen Kenny's departure in November 2023. His record read one win, one draw and two defeats in that period.

The former defender will be hoping to help his country qualify for Euro 2028 which will be played on home soil across the Republic of Ireland, England, Scotland and Wales.

O'Shea is Republic of Ireland assistant head coach - a role he has held since August 2024

#1686. Mikel Arteta shuts down Arsenal team news loophole exposed by Christos Tzolis

By Naim Beneddra | 20 Nov 2026 18:48

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has confirmed that new measures have been introduced to prevent players from accidentally revealing confidential team news through Fantasy Premier League (FPL).

The decision follows an incident involving Christos Tzolis, whose selections in the popular fantasy football game offered an unexpected insight into his availability ahead of Arsenal's Premier League victory over Liverpool earlier this month.

According to The Athletic, Arsenal players have been banned from selecting themselves or their teammates in their FPL squads, reducing the risk of injuries and potential starting line-ups being disclosed before official announcements.

Arteta confirmed the intervention during Friday's press conference ahead of Saturday's trip to Newcastle United, stressing that protecting information about his squad was essential to maintaining trust within the club.

The development is particularly interesting given that Sports Mole was among the outlets to highlight Tzolis's revealing Fantasy Premier League decisions before Arsenal's visit to Anfield on November 1.

Tzolis had been sidelined for approximately a month with a hamstring injury, missing six consecutive Arsenal matches before the trip to Liverpool.

Although Arteta had confirmed that the Greek international had returned to training, his involvement at Anfield remained uncertain.

However, the winger provided a significant indication of his fitness through his own Fantasy Premier League account.

Tzolis transferred himself into his team and selected himself as captain, effectively doubling the points he would earn if he made a successful return.

The decision attracted attention because fantasy managers generally avoid selecting injured players, particularly when using the captaincy on an individual who might not feature.

Sports Mole had already identified the potential significance of those choices in its November 1 report on Tzolis's Fantasy Premier League injury clues.

The same report noted that the former Norwich City winger had retained Riccardo Calafiori in his fantasy squad despite the defender also facing questions over his fitness.

Both players subsequently started at Anfield, where Arsenal secured a 1-0 victory.

Tzolis's activity attracted further attention in the following gameweek.

Ahead of Arsenal's home meeting with Hull City on November 7, the 24-year-old reportedly activated his wildcard, allowing him to make unlimited transfers, and removed every Arsenal player from his fantasy team.

Among those transferred out were Tzolis himself, Calafiori and Ezri Konsa.

Those decisions did not establish who would or would not start against Hull, but they demonstrated how closely players' fantasy activity could be monitored for potential clues.

Tzolis has also previously spoken openly about his enthusiasm for the game.

After Arsenal's opening-day victory over Coventry City, he discussed the points he had accumulated through his own performance, revealing that he had selected himself as captain.

What initially appeared to be a harmless aspect of the player's enjoyment of football has now prompted a response from his manager.

Asked whether he had addressed the issue with his players, Arteta confirmed that discussions had taken place involving Tzolis and other members of the squad.

"With Christos, with the squad and with my kids as well," the Arsenal manager said.

"They're constantly asking me about this as well, because they want to know. It's a topic."

Arteta acknowledged that the popularity of Fantasy Premier League had created a relatively new challenge for clubs seeking to protect information about their players.

"These are the kind of things that are happening in our society right now," he explained.

"It's something new. We haven't dealt with it before and we need to put new things in place."

The Spaniard then emphasised the importance of maintaining confidentiality within the dressing room and coaching staff.

"The confidentiality is something critical because it's about trust and what you're trying to do, and that should be kept as a huge secret."

Arteta added that measures would be taken to prevent further incidents and subsequently confirmed that restrictions were already in place.

The reported policy does not prevent Arsenal players from participating in Fantasy Premier League altogether.

Instead, it specifically targets the selection of Arsenal footballers in their own fantasy teams, limiting the possibility that transfers or captaincy choices reveal information unavailable to opponents and supporters.

Arsenal are not the first Premier League club to confront the problem.

Chelsea faced similar concerns in October after fantasy accounts associated with players and staff appeared to offer clues about Joao Pedro's injury before his absence against Tottenham Hotspur became public.

The Brazilian had reportedly been removed from several fantasy teams ahead of that fixture, prompting speculation about his availability.

Chelsea subsequently warned staff about the risks of revealing confidential information through the game.

For Arsenal, the issue is especially relevant as Arteta attempts to maintain his side's position at the top of the Premier League.

The Gunners travel to Newcastle on Saturday with a five-point advantage over their nearest challengers, and the manager will be keen to avoid giving opponents unnecessary information about his selection decisions.

Tzolis's fantasy activity may have provided an early indication of his return against Liverpool, but Arsenal's new restrictions are designed to ensure that future team news emerges through official channels rather than virtual football transfers.

#1684. Arsenal play like the champions they are as title defence starts with a bang

Mentally liberated and physically rested, Arsenal began the new Premier League campaign with a performance befitting champions. Gone are the anxieties of last season, when the title race gnawed away at their minds and bodies. Gone are the pressures of chasing a first Premier League trophy in more than two decades. Arsenal look slick, refreshed and hungry for more.

“Champions of England, we know what we are,” sang the home supporters in this thrashing of promoted Coventry City. The players moved with the same energy and confidence, as they dominated every aspect of this match against Frank Lampard’s side.

There will, of course, be many tougher games than this one over the course of the season. But there can be no doubt that Arsenal are settled and strong. Everywhere Coventry looked, they saw world-class opponents who knew exactly what to do and where to be. This was Coventry’s first Premier League match since 2001 and it was a reminder, as if one was needed, of the size of the gulf between England’s top two divisions. Thankfully for Lampard, his season will not be decided by matches against teams of Arsenal’s quality.

As it was in last weekend’s Community Shield victory over Manchester City, Mikel Arteta’s side purred and flowed in attack. The rejuvenated Martin Odegaard scored again, as did his close friend Kai Havertz. Bukayo Saka also struck, easing any lingering concerns about his fitness. Both Saka and Declan Rice, who endured such draining campaigns last year, looked sharp.

"The champions are on their way!" Kai Havertz sweeps home from the edge of the box to give Arsenal an early lead against Coventry 👏 pic.twitter.com/SNtrMSPkYJ

There was also another promising performance by new signing Christos Tzolis, while midfield dynamo Myles Lewis-Skelly continued where he left off at the end of last season: winning tackles, spinning past opponents and firing up the home crowd. New face Bruno Guimarães, absent through injury for a few days, was certainly not needed here.

“They know how to do it,” Arteta said of his players. “They know what they have to do. There was a lot to like in the performance. The manner we started the game, with such domination, clarity, understanding and flow, it was really impressive. At this level the players have to be decisive. They were certainly decisive today.”

Coventry had attempted to irritate Arsenal with physicality and direct passes, but it never looked likely to work, despite the best efforts of strikers Ellis Sims and Taiwo Awoniyi. They will not be the first team to struggle against Arsenal’s defenders, and this will not be the first occasion in which their goalkeeper Carl Rushworth is kept busy.

“Arsenal were the best team in the league last year and they showed it,” Lampard said. “They played like it. The noise here at the start of the game, it was different. I remember that noise. It’s different to the Championship.”

"They played like champions" 🏆Frank Lampard said Coventry will learn lessons after their 3-0 opening day defeat to Arsenal ❌ pic.twitter.com/wqA2kngUVt

Before this opening match, Arteta had objected to the idea that Arsenal were planning to “defend” their title. Instead, he said, they are going to “attack” the Premier League once again. It was a classic Arteta-ism, but the manager’s meaning was clear: he wants his team to be aggressive, inventive and courageous. Perhaps more so than in the second half of last season, when their defending was a greater strength than their attacking.

If that was a case of Arteta talking the talk, then his players happily followed it up by walking the walk here. Arsenal played with an unmistakable swagger, as if they simply knew there would only be one outcome against a group of Coventry players with limited experience at this level.

The energy of the home supporters, as buoyant as you might expect following last season’s triumph, undoubtedly helped Arsenal. There were none of the nerves that defined the run-in in the spring, with the fans instead in a partying mood from the moment new signing Ezri Konsa was introduced to the Emirates Stadium before kick-off.

The opening goal took only 15 minutes to arrive, as Havertz swept in an accurate finish from Riccardo Calafiori’s low cross. It has been a good summer for Havertz, who missed so much of last season with injury but has found some rhythm over the past few months. Including friendlies and his performances for Germany at the World Cup, this was his 10th goal in his last 17 appearances.

Coventry have invested in some powerful, commanding players this summer, but there were signs that the physical battle was proving difficult for Lampard’s side. Caleb Yirenkyi is their new club-record signing in midfield, but he was brutally thrown to the floor by Lewis-Skelly in the first half.

Saka’s goal was the result of a quick cross by Tzolis, the new £34m winger who has made such an exciting start to his Arsenal career. The Greek forward was the star of the first half, constantly making things happen, and his delivery was diverted into Saka’s path after 23 minutes.

"Saka couldn't miss!"Arsenal are cruising against Coventry as Bukayo Saka fires home from close range 💥 pic.twitter.com/er411Bi1wh

Odegaard showed in the Community Shield that he is in a more confident place than the last campaign, when he constantly battled injuries, and his early-season form continued here. His goal was scruffy, bobbled in off the right foot, but his all-round performance was typically smooth. With two goals in two games, he has already beaten his tally from last season.

"It's a top finish I would say" 😂Martin Odegaard reacts to his goal against Coventry! pic.twitter.com/mciFfZ6Fhx

From there, the game was over. Arsenal could remove Saka, Rice and Odegaard, safe in the knowledge that their work was done. A comfortable night for the champions, and the perfect start.

"How are you going to keep everyone happy? Winning." 🔥Mikel Arteta reveals his secret for keeping his full squad content after Arsenal's 3-0 win against Coventry 👀 pic.twitter.com/IarLijhd6I

"I think we can do even better to be fair" Martin Odegaard reflects on Arsenal's win over Coventry in the first game of the season 💭 pic.twitter.com/nB2YW83VlE

It’s all over in the capital and Arsenal have started their reign as Premier League champions with a confident and assured three-goal victory over newly-promoted Coventry. Havertz, Saka and Odegaard were all on target in a flawless team performance from Arteta’s men. It’s been a tough evening for Lampard’s side, who simply couldn’t handle Arsenal.

FULL-TIME: Arsenal cruise to victory against Coventry on the opening day of the new season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/ctybTEor9J

There will be four minutes of added time to round this game off. Merino shoots from long range and aims for the bottom corner, but Rushworth dives to his left and makes the stop.

Awoniyi tries to make a run in behind Arsenal’s defence and latch onto Hamer’s pass. The striker is hauled to the ground by Mosquera, who is lucky to escape a booking. The resulting delivery is smacked straight out of play by Torp. That is such a disappointing cross.

Torp swings a cross into Rudoni, who makes a run from deep. Rudoni meets the delivery, but his glancing header is straight at Raya. It’s Coventry’s best chance of the match but they’ve failed to convert it. Arsenal’s clean sheet remains intact.

Arteta makes his fifth and final substitution as Calafiori, who recorded the assist for Arsenal’s opener, is withdrawn for Hincapie.

Lampard responds with his own alteration, bringing Hamer on for Tchaouna.

Coventry are still waiting for their first shot on target this evening. Arsenal are seeing this game out with exemplary professionalism.

Odegaard and Tzolis are the next players to leave the field. Eze and World Cup winner Merino are on as their replacements. Arteta’s substitutions tonight have underlined Arsenal’s tremendous squad depth, and that is without the involvement of both Guimaraes and Konsa.

Lewis-Skelly tries to slide a pinpoint pass through to Calafiori, in an attempt to recreate Arsenal’s opening goal from their Community Shield triumph. It nutmegs Torp, but Rushworth makes a quick dash off his line to collect the ball and eliminate any danger.

Lampard adds some fresh legs and orders a double change. Awoniyi, who makes his Coventry debut, and Rudoni are on, with Simms and Thomas-Asante taken off.

Here come some Arsenal changes. Rice and Saka depart to loud ovations, with Zubimendi and Madueke on to replace them.

Tzolis motors into the Coventry penalty area once again and picks out Havertz, who makes a intelligent run across the six-yard box. Before he can cross or shoot, Thomas sprints over to make an interception.

The visitors then fail to clear a corner and Tzolis slams a low, powerful effort at goal. Rushworth gets down low and spills it, but Thomas is there to hack it away.

Lampard makes the first change of the match for either side as Torp replaces Yirenkyi, whose endured a difficult debut in central midfield for his new side.

Odegaard is enjoying himself out there this evening. Just as he did against Manchester City, he’s playing with such authority, purpose and confidence.

The ball breaks to Tzolis who unleashes a venomous effort at goal. It takes a big deflection and flies out for a corner.

Van Ewijk attempts to find Simms with a chipped cross towards the back post, but it’s marginally over the striker’s head as Coventry step up their search to pull a goal back.

Coventry are feeling the full effects of the stark difference in levels between Championship and Premier League. Arsenal look streets ahead at the moment.

Welcome back to the Premier League, Coventry... It’s been a chastening opening 27 minutes for Lampard’s side.

Van Ewijk fails to clear his lines and he’s closed down by Tzolis. The ball ricochets into Calafiori’s path and the left back picks out Havertz with a low cross.

Coventry get us under way and the newly-promoted side have won an early corner, which is comfortably dealt with by Arsenal’s defence.

The club’s most successful campaign of his time at Arsenal was also the most frustrating one for Odegaard as an individual.

Last season, Arsenal clinched a much-anticipated Premier League title for the first time in 22 years and are the favourites to lift the trophy for a second successive season. Mikel Arteta’s side have recently claimed the Community Shield and look like they mean business.

Arsenal are clearly not resting on their laurels in their bid to win another top-flight title, having strengthened their squad this summer with the signings of Bruno Guimarães, Christos Tzolis and Ezri Konsa.

Arteta looks raring to go and ready to mount another title charge.

After last season’s Championship by a whopping 95 points under Frank Lampard’s management, Coventry head into their first Premier League campaign since suffering relegation from the competition in 2001.

Coventry were playing in the fourth tier as recently as 2017, so lining up against the Premier League holders is a full-circle moment for the club and supporters that is richly deserved.

"I loved it, I loved driving here, feeling the atmosphere, the fans" Frank Lampard on what tonight means for him and Coventry 😍Watch live here: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/077Bga2Z4W

On Friday night, at the home of champions Arsenal, Coventry officially begin a new chapter back in the Premier League and expectations will be high. The man responsible for that tidal wave of optimism is Lampard, their promotion hero.

He has proved a transformative appointment since arriving in November 2024, and the former England and Chelsea captain is relishing the chance to rattle some cages.

His return is a feel-good story and Lampard has a point to prove. He admits that the desire to upset his detractors drives him on. “I’ve got experience of the Premier League and hopefully I can get that across to the players,” he said.

“The club has been out of this division for 25 years so of course it’s exciting. We want to challenge and we want to do well. I’m pleased that we’re here and you want to work at the top. We’re very focused on the job.”

Arsenal ruined Enzo Maresca’s first competitive outing as Man City’s new manager in the club’s first match without Pep Guardiola. It was one-way traffic as Arsenal cruised to a resounding 3-0 win to lift the Community Shield in Cardiff.

Riccardo Calafiori opened the scoring just 23 seconds after he was brilliantly played in by Myles Lewis-Skelly’s defence-splitting pass. Arsenal doubled their lead before the half-hour mark through Kai Havertz’s close-range header and Martin Odegaard added a sumptuously taken third shortly after the interval.

The Premier League holders were in a ruthless mood and completely overran their opponents. Christos Tzolis grabbed two assists out on the left wing, Bruno Guimarães produced a typically commanding performance in the first half and Odegaard controlled proceedings with his creativity.

It was an early taste of silverware for Mikel Arteta’s men, who are the overwhelming favourites to retain their Premier League crown.

To soften the blow of Bruno Guimaraes’ absence from tonight’s squad due to injury, the Premier League holders can rejoice over the signing of Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa for over £50m.

Good evening and welcome to the Emirates Stadium, where the Premier League champions begin the defence of their title. Or, as Mikel Arteta prefers to put it, their “attack” on a new season. A classic Arteta-ism.

The assault starts tonight against Coventry City but our understanding is that Arsenal will be without new £75m midfielder Bruno Guimaraes. We believe the Brazilian has picked up an injury, and it’s not currently clear how severe it might be. Clearly, this is a blow for Arteta. But they should still have enough to get past promoted Coventry… shouldn’t they? We’ll find out soon enough.

Meanwhile, Arteta has said he and his players should relish being Premier League title favourites and the role of the hunted rather than the hunter.

“In the last three seasons, at some point we were first and at some point we were chasing. And you never know what is better,” Arteta said. “But if you give me the choice, I want to be first. I want to be hunted, and I want to be in control of our future, rather than depending on somebody else.”

#1681. Ajax vs. ADO Den Haag - prediction, team news, lineups

By Seye Omidiora | 20 Nov 2026 19:45, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 19:50

ADO Den Haag travel to the Johan Cruyff Arena on Sunday, looking to end their six-match losing run against Amsterdam giants Ajax in this weekend's matchday 13 Eredivisie encounter.

Their 15-year wait for victory in this fixture further underlines the magnitude of the task facing Maurice Steijn's side.

Ajax entered the recent international break wondering what might have been after surrendering a two-goal advantage at FC Twente.

Goals from Tolu Arokodare and substitute Rayane Bounida seemingly put Michel's men home and hosed heading into the final half-hour, only for Dies Janse to score an own goal and Wout Weghorst to punish his former side with a penalty in the fifth minute of second-half stoppage time.

That equaliser denied De Joden the opportunity to finish gameweek 12 atop the Eredivisie table, leaving them level on 25 points with Feyenoord and one behind leaders PSV Eindhoven, who are chasing a fourth consecutive title.

Looking to move on from that setback, the Amsterdam giants welcome ADO to the capital aiming to secure a seventh consecutive victory over the promoted side.

Further encouraging the hosts is their longstanding unbeaten record in this fixture, with a 3-2 defeat in March 2011 marking Ajax's last loss to this weekend's visitors.

ADO have since gone 20 competitive meetings without a victory in this fixture, losing 15 times to underline their historical inferiority.

As such, it will be intriguing to see how new boss Steijn approaches his first match in charge of the promoted side, who dismissed Robin Peter before the international break following a run of one victory in 11 Eredivisie matches.

There was an immediate lift under Levi Schwiebbe as the second-bottom outfit defeated Sparta Rotterdam 3-1 to move within one point of 16th-placed Telstar in the relegation playoff spot and two of SBV Excelsior.

Back-to-back top-flight victories could therefore lift Den Haag out of the relegation positions, although results elsewhere must also go their way.

Despite the managerial change, ADO's away record offers little encouragement, with the visitors collecting just two points from an available 18 on their travels and failing to score in three of those six matches.

Those figures, coupled with their historical struggles against Ajax, underline the challenge facing Steijn, who is winless in 15 previous encounters with the capital club, losing 11.

Ajax could again be without Julian Brandt this weekend, with the attacking midfielder having not played since going off injured in late October's 1-0 victory over AZ Alkmaar.

If the six-goal Germany international remains sidelined, Arokodare, who has seven goals and one assist, will shoulder much of the attacking responsibility, while Oscar Gloukh offers a creative threat with six assists, including setting up both goals in the 2-2 draw at Twente a fortnight ago.

While Anton Gaaei, like Brandt, will be assessed before Sunday, Michel must manage without Simon Adingra, long-term absentee Kasper Dolberg (knee) and Viktor Tsygankov.

Steijn has fewer injury concerns, although the ADO boss must make do without Alex Pozo and Luka Reischl (groin) this weekend.

Juho Kilo may not score regularly, but the midfielder's passing and creativity make him a standout presence for the visitors.

Nonetheless, the goalscoring burden falls on Nigel Thomas, Yannick Eduardo and Evan Rottier, who have netted four, three and two league goals respectively.

Ter Stegen; Rosa, Bouman, Janse, Wijndal; Amrabat, Baas; Klaassen, Mokio, Gloukh; Arokodare

Nikiema; De Ruijter, Mulder, Waem, Hokke; Kilo, Jimenez; Van Mieghem, Rottier, Hawkins; Thomas

Ajax's late collapse at Twente demonstrated that their defensive concentration remains fallible, offering some hope to an ADO side fresh from scoring three against Sparta.

Nevertheless, Gloukh's creativity and Arokodare's finishing should give Michel's men enough attacking quality to overcome Brandt's potential absence and prolong the visitors' miserable record in this fixture.

Manchester United have reportedly made a key decision on Harry Amass ahead of the January transfer window, as they look to resolve ongoing uncertainty at left-back.

The 19-year-old academy graduate had been linked with a permanent departure from Old Trafford during the summer. However, United now appear ready to protect his future by extending his contract, while leaving open the possibility of another loan move.

With injuries affecting the club’s senior defensive options, Amass’ situation could become increasingly important in the coming months.

According to the Evening Standard, Manchester United are preparing to trigger a 12-month extension clause in Amass’ existing contract.

The decision would give the club greater control over the defender’s future and prevent him from approaching the end of his deal without a resolution.

Amass attracted interest from Burnley during the summer after spending time on loan with Sheffield Wednesday and Norwich City. A permanent exit appeared possible, but United ultimately retained the youngster.

The club’s latest reported decision suggests they are not ready to lose control of a player who remains a promising defensive prospect.

United’s situation at left-back has been complicated by fitness concerns involving Luke Shaw and Patrick Dorgu.

Shaw has struggled with injuries throughout his career, while Dorgu has provided an alternative option when available. Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui can also cover the position, although both are more naturally suited to right-back.

These issues could influence whether Amass stays at Old Trafford or is allowed to leave on loan in January.

Regular first-team football would be valuable for the young defender’s development, but United may be reluctant to weaken their depth while senior players remain unavailable.

A temporary move remains a possibility if United believe Amass would benefit from more regular playing time elsewhere.

His previous loan spells offered opportunities to gain senior experience, although an injury interrupted his time at Norwich City last season.

United must now balance his development against their immediate need for defensive cover. Extending his contract would give the club additional flexibility to make that decision without risking his longer-term value.

The situation could also affect United’s plans for recruiting another left-back, particularly if the club decide they need a more established option.

United’s reported decision to extend Amass’ contract would provide greater security over his future, but it does not guarantee that he will remain in the first-team squad for the rest of the season.

A January loan could still make sense if Shaw and Dorgu are fit enough to provide cover. If injuries continue, however, Amass may have an opportunity to establish himself at Old Trafford.

#1678. Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli needs a statement win to change the narrative around his new-look side

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 13:37 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 13:37 EST, 15 November 2026

While it’s fair to state that the touchpaper has yet to be lit on Sebastien Pocognoli’s tenure, he is hardly the first Scotland manager to discover that the battle for hearts and minds can be a drawn-out affair.

Although Steve Clarke marked the start of his era with an unconvincing win over Cyprus at Hampden in 2019, the Ayrshireman lost his next four games to Russia and Belgium. It would take him 15 months to chalk up what might be considered a statement victory.

That 2-1 win against the Czech Republic in Olomouc in September 2020, in his tenth match in charge, felt like a turning point for the national team and so it proved with qualification for the delayed Euros in the post. But Clarke certainly had to suffer for it.

So for all the frustration felt at Pocognoli’s new-look side failing to hit the straps in the past five matches, we have been here before. And statistically, to date, it’s also been by no means disastrous.

Notwithstanding how ordinary North Macedonia are, the Belgian is actually the first manager since Gordon Strachan in 2013 to win more than one of his first five games in charge. The history books show that Scotland don’t really do fast starts when there’s a new man at the helm.

Nonetheless, it would be hard to overstate the significance of Pocognoli seeing it all spectacularly come together as the Nations League campaign concludes in St Gallen tomorrow.

Scotland captain Andy Robertson and John McGinn enjoy a light-hearted moment in training.

Sebastien Pocognoli is one of many Scotland managers who have made slow starts in the job.

Switzerland boss Murat Yakin will give some of his fringe players a chance against Scotland.

Friday’s win over the group whipping boys was certainly deserved, yet the performance, particularly in the first half, was hardly scintillating.

Even those who are prepared to be patient with Pocognoli would have been concerned at the lack of tempo and imagination in the general play in the first period.

Weren’t we told that he would bring a radically different approach to Clarke? Yet there was scant evidence on show of the ultra-offensive, high-pressing style which was billed in the brochure.

While a markedly better second half yielded a welcome first home win for the 39-year-old, no one left the arena clicking their heels at what they’d witnessed. This remains very much a work in progress.

What can be said with some certainty, however, is that the players are on board with the grand plan. When they faced the media last week, it was noticeable that Scott McTominay, Andy Robertson and John McGinn all praised the new man’s methods and ideas and predicted that they will bear fruit in the fullness of time.

You get a sense when experienced players are reading empty platitudes from a prepared script. Yet the words of the leadership group felt truly authentic on that occasion.

While Pocognoli will obviously have welcomed them, it’s not statements of support from senior figures which he needs to keep the Tartan Army onside. It’s positive results.

Come what may against Switzerland tomorrow, Scotland don’t have a match until March. That’s an awful long time to reflect if it doesn’t go well.

What Pocognoli and the travelling fans wouldn’t give for that seismic win to shift the narrative and engender a greater sense of optimism ahead of the Euro qualifiers.

Strachan’s first big scalp arrived at the fourth time of asking when a Robert Snodgrass goal sealed an unlikely win away to Croatia. Such unexpected outcomes can have a galvanising effect.

Friday’s narrow win over North Macedonia did keep the possibility alive of Scotland finishing second in Group B1, but few would be sticking their house on that yet coming to pass.

With head-to-head rather than goal difference counting if sides are locked on the same number of points, Pocognoli’s men must beat the Swiss then hope that Slovenia don’t win in Skopje. Stranger things have happened, but not too many.

In all likelihood, Scotland will finish third and be a pot three team when the draw for Euro 2028 is made in Belfast on December 6. Yet, it’s still vital that they conclude this campaign with – at the very least – a display which offers grounds for optimism.

This was always going to be the toughest assignment of the six. In the summer, the Swiss reached the last eight of the World Cup for the first time since 1954, only losing in extra-time to Argentina. That remains their only defeat this year.

They’ve hardly missed a beat in the Nations League, winning four games and drawing one, to comfortably secure promotion to the top tier.

Even though they were given a helping hand by Jack Hendry’s early red card as they won 3-0 at Hampden in September, they looked a level above Pocognoli’s men.

‘We reached all of our goals,’ said coach Murat Yakin.

‘Maybe we could have done even more at the World Cup, but we created history by reaching the quarter-finals.

‘I am happy with our playing style. There’s been good development and we have integrated new players.’

The hope for Scotland stems from the fact that Yakin is compelled to give some fringe players an opportunity to shine in St Gallen.

Inter Milan’s Manuel Akanji has become the latest big name to withdraw through injury. Johan Manzambi, Dan Ndoye and Granit Xhaka were already out.

Even then, the task for the visitors remains formidable. The only defeat for the Swiss in their past 11 games on home soil came at the hands of Germany.

‘It has happened a few times already,’ Yakin said of the injury situation.

‘But we will make sure we get a good level of players on to the pitch. It’s a good thing we have won the group already. It’s now an opportunity to make changes.

‘It doesn’t make sense to wait. We have enough opportunities and possibilities.’

It feels like a night for Pocognoli to proceed with caution. A fairly assured display against North Macedonia means Ryan Porteous, Luke Graham and Kieran Tierney will probably be asked to go again as a back-three.

Given his defensive diligence, Aaron Hickey would be favoured to displace Ben Gannon-Doak on the right flank.

As on Friday, Billy Gilmour and Lewis Ferguson should play behind John McGinn and Scott McTominay with Che Adams leading the line.

On the occasion when he’ll become Scotland’s most capped player with 103 appearances, it’s to be hoped Andy Robertson has a night to remember.

‘What can I say about him?’ added Yakin. ‘He’s a fantastic player, who has also constantly carried the team or the nation of Scotland.

‘The best players should be on the pitch and we’re happy to compete with him. It’s a nice mark for him, and in that sense, congratulations.’

#1677. New heights and same problems: How Milan stars fared in the November international break

With just a few days until the return of AC Milan action, the international break is now done. Let’s take a look at how the internationals fared.

Whether you love it or you hate it, the international break is now over and players are trickling back into Milanello. Even those who didn’t head away are only just really returning, with Ruben Amorim offering the squad a week off.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

So, let’s look at what Amorim has returning, with several things to shout about…

Christian Pulisic probably leaves the break as the star of the week(s). His brace against Haiti helped secure a place in the CONCACAF Nations League semifinals, and he then rounded it off with a bicycle kick in the second leg.

After missing the penultimate international break of the season – to ensure he was fully back to fitness – he’s quickly reminded everyone of how important he can be for club and country, scoring his seventh goal of the season in only 13 games.

He’s on fire and there are no signs of him slowing down anytime soon.

You’d then have to speak about Diego Moreira, who has left the international break – somehow – with more praise than he started it with. He starred in Belgium’s 2-1 win against Turkiye and then followed that up with a goal against Italy.

It gets to a point where you run out of superlatives to describe a player and his teammates are already at that stage. Both Mark Van Bommel and Koni De Winter have called him crazy (in a good way), with the former even putting him in the same group as Kevin De Bruyne and Jeremy Doku.

He’s become a starter for the Red Devils and it’s difficult to see that changing.

In terms of the Italians, Milan had a few reasons to smile and it starts with Alphadjo Cisse. At first, it seemed he’d been wasted during the break, with Roberto Mancini not calling him up for the game against France.

However, he was given the nod for the second game and got some valuable minutes on the field. As the Rossoneri have become familiar with, he took that chance with both hands, scoring a disallowed goal and winning a penalty in a defeat to Belgium.

He’s shining with confidence currently and long may it continue.

Then, Francesco Camarda is probably at the other end of the scale. He’s clearly not got the most confidence when representing the Diavolo, but returning to the youth level, he shone like he always has.

Against Sankhoun Diawara’s France side, he was excellent. In terms of his hold-up play, finishing and just general performance, he was almost perfect, if not perfect. With a goal to round it off too, he leaves the break with a much-needed confidence boost.

Unfortunately, we can’t say the same for Goncalo Ramos. After Cristiano Ronaldo’s retirement, this was a chance for him to take the star role and prove that he’s going to be the man to ensure things keep ticking.

Instead, he left the break leaving Portugal with more questions than answers, which is a familiar feeling.

He played just shy of 150 minutes during the break and mustered just one shot. It’s not like he provided an assist or any key passes either. In other words, it’s another blank for him and it’s clearly having an effect.

Without a goal in 661 minutes, it’s no shock why the Diavolo are so heavily pursuing a striker ahead of January.

For France, it was a relatively quiet break for Mike Maignan and Adrien Rabiot. Neither performed especially well against Italy in a 3-1 loss at San Siro, though Rabiot was named as the captain for that game. Then, in the second game, Maignan was injured. However, it seems he’ll be fine for this weekend.

Not a lot to shout about for those two, but that’s not necessarily a bad thing either.

For Luka Modric, his minutes were focused in the right areas. He played 14 minutes in a nothing game against England, but was then essential in a 2-1 win against the Czech Republic, which may help them qualify for the latter stages of the Nations League.

It was another strange international break for Ardon Jashari, too. He was given no minutes against Slovenia in a 0-0 draw, but then played the full 90 minutes against Scotland, where they won 4-0. He made 76 passes from 90 touches, so he had some involvement. However, he’s still a way away from being a dictator of the team, as it was hoped he’d be.

Davide Bartesaghi, Christian Comotto and Sankhoun Diawara were all given valuable minutes during the break. Finally, Pervis Estupinan played 36 minutes over the break. He returns without any injuries and that’s all there is to really say about his past fortnight.

#1673. Coventry vs. Crystal Palace: How Frank Lampard compares to Thomas Frank as relegation warning sent

By Ben Knapton | 20 Nov 2026 20:00, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 20:00

Coventry City vs. Crystal Palace is the sort of match that will keep Frank Lampard's men in the Premier League if they can prevail, an ex-Sky Blues striker has told Sports Mole.

Coventry host Crystal Palace in the Eagles' first fixture under new head coach Thomas Frank, who takes over from Pierre Sage with the Eagles languishing at the bottom of the Premier League table.

The hosts, meanwhile, are three places and two points better off in the relative safety of 17th spot, having taken nine points from their opening 10 games of their first top-flight season in 25 years.

Two of Coventry's three league triumphs this season have come at the CBS Arena, both against bottom-half rivals in Newcastle United and Sunderland, although Fulham and Hull City have also got the better of them in front of their own fans.

Former Coventry striker Mark Hateley - who scored 27 goals in a century of appearances for the Sky Blues - is fearing a new manager bounce for Palace, but warned his old club that this type of match could dictate their survival chances.

“You always get that bounce from a new manager," Hateley said. "You get it for one, two, three games, and then it starts to wear off. Thomas Frank is a proven tactician who sees things very quickly within a team.

“Palace still have a really decent side with decent players, so I think he'll be in and about it quickly, and you'll see a style of play that he gets from what he sees in that group of players. Whether it lasts all the way through, I don't know, but I think he'll fix Palace into a side that will be OK.

“Coventry are the other side. They've got to survive this year and build for the next two years: survival, survival, survival. Palace will know how to do it; they've got good enough players. But these are the games Coventry should be looking to win. These are the games that keep you in the league.”

Saturday's match will mark the first meeting between Coventry and Crystal Palace since the 2011-12 Championship season, when the Sky Blues lost 2-1 away before holding the Eagles to a 1-1 draw at home.

Coventry earned their most recent victory against Crystal Palace shortly beforehand, prevailing 2-1 in February 2011 thanks to goals from Richard Wood and Marlon King.

Taking data across all competitions from Lampard's Coventry tenure so far and Frank's lengthy spell at Brentford from 2018 to 2025, the statistics somewhat favour the Chelsea legend.

Indeed, Lampard boasts more points per game, more goals scored per match and fewer goals conceded per match, while also winning one trophy in the form of the Championship.

However, those numbers must certainly be taken with a pinch of salt given Frank's substantially longer spell at Brentford, and the Dane's four full seasons in the top flight after winning promotion with the Bees.

Lampard's Coventry have nevertheless shown promising signs after he also succeeded in keeping Everton afloat in the top flight, though, so Saturday's edition of Frank vs. Frank is a challenging one to call.

Mark Hateley was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of London.bet.
